economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Two-pass public-evidence and corrective gap-closure audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, valuation-notice, tax-statement and payment records; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental, workforce and utility-regulatory sources; federal environmental, workplace-safety and county-economic access points; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Twenty-three quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; five exact-parcel taxable-market-value stocks for payable 2023-2027; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. The exact parcel statements crosswalk the 2023-2025 city-table values to parcel 30.0590020, but the duplicate value concepts are alternative assessor presentations and are not additive. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. Parcel taxes span all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit. No synthesis fragment is added because candidate-by-candidate review found no defensible project inputs for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, quantified community transfers, or a causal county employment, wage or GDP effect. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Corrective public-evidence and candidate-modeling audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor and ownership history, Treasurer, Accela permits, rights-of-way, planning, air quality, budgets and financial reports; Nevada incentive, tax and utility-regulatory sources; operator, SEC, workforce, supplier and contractor materials; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations remain after the corrective pass; no wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audit, later facility, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, company-wide employment or parcel-transfer price is recast as NAP7 contribution. One modeled synthesis is retained under the last-resort modeling gate: the fiscal-year 2027 real-property bill defines an exactly same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold. It is not actual public cost, collected revenue, jurisdictional receipt or a net fiscal result. Candidate models for investment, construction, suppliers, operations, resources, community benefits, net fiscal effects and county employment, GDP and wages were rejected for missing facility inputs, incompatible scope or timing, overlap, non-identification or lack of decision relevance. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional receipts, actual project-attributable public costs and net fiscal impact remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every sourced amount remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records preserve Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; assessor and tax records provide parcel-value stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permits provide discrete administrative values and contractors; MEPA and MassDEP records establish supporting electric work and permit-listed generators; and two recipient records verify separate community contributions. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Source-family gap closure found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility-upgrade cost, annual water or wastewater series, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. One last-resort synthesis survives: the exact FY2026 real-property-bill amount is reused only as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, not as observed cost, collected revenue or a net fiscal result; all other contribution and GDP, employment and wage candidates are rejected individually in the project updates. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective two-pass public-evidence audit of Apple Mesa at 3740 S Signal Butte Road. The selected IM3 object is one 1,338,261-square-foot mapped building footprint, while the assessor describes a 1,255,156-square-foot Computer Center improvement and the permit, tax, utility, FTZ and operator sources generally cover the whole converted facility or related supporting infrastructure. The account therefore retains campus, company-county and supporting-infrastructure facts as unallocated unless a source supplies a narrower crosswalk. Twenty-five direct observations are added: the assessor floor-area fact and twenty-four completed positive-valuation Apple-era permits omitted from the prior account. Permit valuations are administrative amounts and related permits or addenda are not summed. All direct tax, payment, investment, electricity, renewable-capacity and projection records already in the base account remain; no unsupported zero is introduced. Direct water use, wastewater volume, utility bills, facility payroll, worker residence, local supplier payments, realized IOC relief, project-attributable community payments, marginal public-service costs and causal county outcomes remain unresolved. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective primary-source audit adds current Andale parcel assessment, contractor-reported campus floor area, and two recipient- or government-reported Meta community grants. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. Campus-wide facts remain unallocated to the selected inventory building, overlapping community amounts are not added together, and unavailable supplier, payroll, utility-billing, discharge, generator, and marginal-service-cost amounts remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Apple's Washoe County data-center campus at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West and its 2024 expansion application. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. No campus total is allocated to the selected mapped building; the four-building campus, later buildout cases, downtown Reno warehouse, supporting renewable projects, fire-station parcel, and more-than-200-person support statement are not collapsed into one footprint. No Switch Citadel or Storey County amount enters this fragment. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Corrective public-evidence and last-resort modeling audit for the State Farm data center at 24400 West Valley Parkway in Olathe, Kansas. The account adds the exact-address Kansas HPIP FY2020 capital-investment entry to the City permit and SEC property evidence while keeping the HPIP amount, permit values, SEC estimated cumulative capital spending, parcel assessments, tax bills and tax payments distinct and non-additive. The search trail covers parcel and fiscal records, construction and suppliers, operations and workforce, incentives, utility and environmental regulation, community activity, planning, public costs and county outcomes. No site-level employment, payroll, supplier payment, community transfer, metered electricity or water, claimed incentive amount, actual marginal public-service cost, net fiscal position or attributable county effect is inferred from public material. prj_study_im3_building_00626785488: Corrective two-pass public-evidence audit for the individual 654,433-square-foot IM3-mapped building footprint within Meta's Los Lunas data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW. The search matrix covered original-campus chronology and financing; Village budgets, audits, LEDA, development, planning, permit, traffic, fire, water and wastewater records; Valencia County assessor, treasurer and clerk access; New Mexico economic-development, workforce, court, Construction Industries Division, Public Regulation Commission and Environment Department materials; PNM filings; Meta operator and SEC materials; contractors and suppliers; community recipients; and federal county GDP, employment and wage data through September 6, 2026. Eighteen direct observations are retained, all at unallocated campus, company-county or supporting-infrastructure scope because no public source crosswalks the selected IM3 footprint to a separately named building, permit, parcel, workforce, utility meter or fiscal account. Current campus totals of more than 400 supported jobs and more than $6.2 million of direct community funding, plus a recipient-reported donation floor, are retained as overlapping campus or county facts; Meta's current $2.5-billion and Fortis's $2.2-billion campus investment figures are excluded from records because they span later expansion. The 2021 two-building expansion, 2023 expansion load, 2025 AI expansion, off-site renewable projects, tenant equipment and other Meta facilities remain outside the boundary. Each of the eight contribution categories and each of GDP, employment and wage outcomes was evaluated separately; no model passed because allocation, timing, treatment or outcome attribution prerequisites remain absent. No synthesis fragment is added. Building-level capital expenditure, permits and fees, payroll, resident employment, supplier payments, metered electricity and water, utility bills, tax or PILOT payments, cash value of realized abatements, public-service costs and net fiscal results remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. Opening-day and current operator specifications remain separate dated snapshots because the reported area and capacity changed. The county portal now establishes a 2021-2025 parcel-tax principal series, but not Expedient's incidence under the lease. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Google Clarksville in Montgomery County, Tennessee. The review covered Tennessee Comptroller industrial-development-board PILOT filings for 2019-2025; the Montgomery County assessor GIS parcel service and Trustee tax-bill portal; parcel-linked stormwater files; Clarksville-Montgomery County Regional Planning Commission materials; IDB, county-commission and city agenda archives; state and federal environmental portals; operator location, environmental, economic-impact and watershed materials; utility annual reports; and public workforce, contractor, procurement and recipient sources. Fifty-eight incremental quantitative observations are preserved: thirteen annual Foxman LLC estimated-actual-property-value stocks, eighteen account-level appraised-value stocks, eighteen account-level zero tax levies, a realized opening-period employee snapshot, a construction-workforce projection, and seven recipient-specific community contributions. The direct Trustee records resolve the ordinary tax bills as 0%-taxable, zero-assessed-taxable-value, zero-levy bills; they do not resolve the separate contractual PILOT payments left blank in state filings, and the portal's generic paid/zero-balance label is not treated as a cash receipt. The selected inventory key is one building, while parcel, account and environmental evidence is campus or company/county scoped and remains unallocated. Statewide investment and modeled impact totals, shared Alabama-Tennessee renewable capacity, regional watershed contributions, vendor presence without paid-contract evidence, and proposals for later Building 13 work are excluded from canonical project records. A single optional synthesis reproduces the operator's 2024 Montgomery County water-consumption identity at unallocated location scope; no multiplier, supplier-retention, fiscal-net, public-cost, energy, payroll or causal county model is created. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Second-pass public-evidence audit for NTT Silicon Valley SV1 at 1160 Walsh Avenue, Santa Clara. The review reconciles the planning-era 1150 Walsh address to APN 224-58-003; adds the finaled principal permit, its administrative job value, current operator specifications, emergency-generator authorization and the parcel's regular-bill payment history; and leaves supplemental bills separate to avoid double counting. Public sources still do not establish realized site employment or payroll, total project investment, supplier payments, project-specific community transfers, metered resources, or project-attributable public-service costs. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Foundational corrective audit for Digital Crossroad DX-1 at 100 Digital Crossroads Drive, Hammond, Indiana. The selected IM3 building remains the project key, while tax accounts, utility infrastructure, permits, investment, jobs and supplier facts remain at their reported campus, company/county or supporting-infrastructure scopes and are unallocated. The audit adds the previously omitted DX Hammond JV LLC personal-property account, a current IDEM permit equipment snapshot and Indiana DNR confirmation of the transferred water-withdrawal registration; it also corrects the legacy 910.85 MGD transcription to 910.08 MGD. Paid taxes, bills, assessed values, gross distributions, credits, cap savings, permit capacities and permit-listed equipment remain separate and non-additive. No audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payment ledger, local-purchase share, annual-average operating FTE or payroll, recipient-verified community transfer, metered electricity, reported water withdrawal, wastewater discharge, actual emissions, same-scope marginal public-service cost or credible project-attributable county outcome was found. The 43 legacy models are each dispositioned in project updates: two tax-account syntheses are revised and 41 estimates are directed for removal. prj_study_im3_building_01024051963: Corrective source audit for the Meta Eagle Mountain campus and the selected IM3 building footprint in Utah County. Campus, company-county, and supporting-infrastructure observations remain explicitly unallocated to the selected building; later expansion areas and unrelated Eagle Mountain data-center developers are excluded unless a source establishes continuity. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. The audit distinguishes completed IEDA contracts 08-HQJC-030 and 12-HQJP-051 from the 2022 award still in performance; permit valuations remain administrative amounts rather than expenditure; assessed and taxable values remain stocks; bills remain distinct from payments; and community grants remain recipient- and period-specific.
